items.title: Associative graded algebras, bimodules, and internal shifts
items.statement: Over a commutative degree-zero ground ring k, use unital associative Z-graded k-algebras A with 1 in A_0, graded left/right/bimodules with k-central commuting actions, and degree-zero module maps. For any integer r define M{r}_d=M_{d-r}. In the published nonnegative commutative specialization M{r}=M(-r), where M(a)_d=M_{d+a}. Internal degree alone introduces no super sign.

references.title: Alexander Kleshchev, Representation Theory of Symmetric Groups and Related Hecke Algebras (2009), §2.2, printed pp. 6-7
references.locator: §2.2 printed pp.6–7

items.strategy: Check that the shifted action carries A_i M{r}_d into M{r}_{i+d}, and reconcile the two displayed twist conventions by substitution.

items.title: Graded modules with degree-zero maps form an abelian category
items.statement: For any unital associative Z-graded algebra A, the category GrMod_0(A) of graded left A-modules and degree-zero maps is abelian. Kernels, images, cokernels and finite biproducts are computed in each homogeneous degree; a sequence is exact precisely when it is exact degreewise.

references.title: Alexander Kleshchev, Representation Theory of Symmetric Groups and Related Hecke Algebras (2009), §2.2, printed pp. 6-7
references.locator: §2.2 printed p.6

references.title: Stacks Project, Algebra, §10.56, tag 00JL
references.locator: §10.56 opening paragraphs

items.strategy: Restrict a degree-zero map to each component, verify the kernel and image are stable under all homogeneous A_i, and grade the cokernel quotient. Addition and biproducts are degreewise. The ordinary module first-isomorphism map is degree zero and bijective on every component, so coimage-to-image is an isomorphism.
items.proof_strategy: direct

items.title: Graded balanced tensor product and homogeneous Hom
items.statement: For graded compatible right A-module M and left A-module N, grade M⊗_A N by total internal degree i+j on homogeneous m⊗n. For graded left A-modules P,Q set Hom_{A,d}(P,Q)={A-linear maps f with f(P_i)⊆Q_{i+d}} and HOM_A(P,Q)=⊕_{d∈Z}Hom_{A,d}(P,Q). Degree-zero morphisms are Hom_{A,0}. HOM contains finite sums of homogeneous maps and need not equal all ungraded A-linear maps; no Koszul sign follows from internal grading alone.

references.title: Alexander Kleshchev, Representation Theory of Symmetric Groups and Related Hecke Algebras (2009), §2.2, printed pp. 6-7
references.locator: §2.2 printed p.7

items.strategy: Present the tensor as the direct sum of homogeneous tensor generators modulo homogeneous bilinearity and balance relations; compare with the existing ungraded universal quotient. Verify composition adds degrees and that only finite homogeneous sums are admitted to HOM.

items.title: Graded associativity, units, and internal-shift tensor isomorphisms
items.statement: For composable graded bimodules, the ordinary balanced associator and unit maps are degree-zero graded isomorphisms. For integers r,s, the identity on elementary tensors induces M{r}⊗_A N{s}≅(M⊗_A N){r+s}, naturally and compatibly with outer actions.

references.title: Mikhail Khovanov and Paul Seidel, Quivers, Floer Cohomology, and Braid Group Actions, §§2a-2b, author pp. 8-9
references.locator: §2b author p.9

items.strategy: Use the published balanced associator and unit inverses, then check every elementary tensor has matching total degree on both sides. The balancing relation (ma)⊗n=m⊗(an) is homogeneous; identity on tensors gives the shift map and its inverse. No parity signs enter.
items.proof_strategy: direct

items.title: Finite graded projective modules
items.statement: A graded A-module P is graded projective when it is a projective object of GrMod_0(A). It is finite graded projective when it is also finitely generated as an A-module, equivalently generated by a finite homogeneous family. Projectivity is tested only against degree-zero epimorphisms and degree-zero maps; its finite free-summand characterization is the next theorem.

references.title: Alexander Kleshchev, Representation Theory of Symmetric Groups and Related Hecke Algebras (2009), §2.2, printed pp. 6-7
references.locator: §2.2, printed pp.6–7, PDF pp.5–6, from the graded-module paragraph through equation (2.5) and the Cartan-pairing paragraph

items.strategy: Decompose each member of a finite ordinary generating set into finitely many homogeneous components to get a finite homogeneous family. Apply the published projective-object lifting definition in the abelian category proved above.

items.title: Finite graded projectives are finite shifted-free summands
items.statement: A graded left A-module P is finite graded projective if and only if it is a degree-zero direct summand of a finite direct sum of internal shifts A{r_j}. Every finite shifted-free graded module is projective in GrMod_0(A), without an assumption of arbitrary-index choice.

references.title: Alexander Kleshchev, Representation Theory of Symmetric Groups and Related Hecke Algebras (2009), §2.2, printed pp. 6-7

items.strategy: For homogeneous generators p_j of degrees r_j, map the degree-r_j basis vector of A{r_j} to p_j; projectivity splits this finite graded-free epimorphism. Conversely lift finitely many homogeneous basis vectors through any degree-zero epimorphism using finite choice, extend A-linearly, and restrict the lift to a summand. The summand is finite generated as image of the finite free module.
items.proof_strategy: direct

items.title: Bimodule tensor exactness and preservation of finite projectives have separate hypotheses
items.statement: For a graded B–A bimodule M, M⊗_A− is exact on graded left A-modules if M is flat as an underlying right A-module. Independently, it carries finite graded projective left A-modules to finite graded projective left B-modules if M is finite graded projective as a left B-module. Neither hypothesis is asserted to imply the other.

items.strategy: For exactness forget grading, apply the published right-flat definition, and recover degreewise exactness from homogeneous tensor maps. For projectives write X as a retract of finitely many A{r_j}; tensor the split maps, identify M⊗_A A{r_j} with M{r_j}, and use finite direct sums and retracts of finite graded projectives. The two B witnesses test independence.
items.proof_strategy: direct

items.title: Associative and graded bimodule tensor–Hom adjunction
items.statement: For a graded B–A bimodule M, graded left A-module X and graded left B-module Y, currying gives a natural bijection Hom_{B,0}(M⊗_A X,Y)≅Hom_{A,0}(X,HOM_B(M,Y)), with left A-action (a·f)(m)=f(ma). For ungraded module maps there is separately Hom_B^{ungr}(M⊗_A X,Y)≅Hom_A^{ungr}(X,Hom_B^{ungr}(M,Y)); HOM_B is the direct sum of homogeneous maps, not all ungraded maps.

references.title: Stacks Project, Algebra, §10.12, tag 00CV
references.locator: §10.12 Lemma 8

references.title: Alexander Kleshchev, Representation Theory of Symmetric Groups and Related Hecke Algebras (2009), §2.2, printed pp. 6-7
references.locator: §2.2, printed pp.6–7, PDF pp.5–6, from the graded-module paragraph through equation (2.5) and the Cartan-pairing paragraph

items.strategy: Curry F to x↦(m↦F(m⊗x)); check B-linearity, A-linearity via (a f)(m)=f(ma), internal degree, and naturality. Conversely evaluate an A-linear map X→HOM_B(M,Y), use finite homogeneous support of each value, and verify (ma)⊗x=m⊗ax; the two constructions are inverse on elementary tensors. Repeat with full ungraded Hom for the ungraded adjunction. The published commutative adjunction is not used as the general-ring proof.
items.proof_strategy: direct

items.title: Restriction and extension along a graded algebra map
items.statement: For a degree-zero unital k-algebra map f:A→B, restriction GrMod_0(B)→GrMod_0(A) is exact and extension B⊗_A− is its left adjoint. Extension is exact if B is flat as a right A-module, and always preserves finite graded projectives. Restriction preserves finite graded projectives if B is finite graded projective as a left A-module.

items.strategy: Define the B–A bimodule B using f. Restriction preserves homogeneous kernels and cokernels. Specialize the graded tensor–Hom adjunction and identify HOM_B(B,Y) with restricted Y by evaluation at 1. Apply the two clauses of the tensor theorem for flatness/projectivity; for unconditional extension of projectives, tensor a finite A-shifted-free retract and obtain a finite B-shifted-free retract. For restriction, restrict a finite B-shifted-free retract and use the assumed A-projectivity of B.
items.proof_strategy: direct

title: Graded Bimodules and Tensor Functors — Examples

items.title: An internal shift reverses the published commutative twist parameter
items.statement: For k[x] with deg x=1, the monomial x^j has degree j+2 in k[x]{2}, whereas it has degree j−2 in the published twist k[x](2). Thus k[x]{2}=k[x](−2) as graded modules, and the internal shift does not alter multiplication or differential signs.

references.title: Stacks Project, Algebra, §10.56, tag 00JL
references.locator: §10.56 opening definitions through Lemma 10.56.1 and its proof, lines 16–36 of the HTML full text

references.locator: §2.2, printed pp.6–7, PDF pp.5–6, from the graded-module paragraph through equation (2.5) and the Cartan-pairing paragraph

items.strategy: Compute k[x]{2}_d=k[x]_{d−2} and k[x](2)_d=k[x]_{d+2}; list degrees of 1,x,x² in both and verify the identity of k[x]{2} and k[x](−2) component by component.
items.proof_strategy: direct

items.title: A right-flat tensor bimodule can have nonprojective output
items.statement: Let k be a field, A=k, B=k[ε]/(ε²) with trivial internal grading, and M=k with left B-action through B→k and ordinary right k-action. M is right A-flat, so M⊗_k− is exact, but M⊗_k k≅k is not projective as a left B-module.

references.title: Mikhail Khovanov and Paul Seidel, Quivers, Floer Cohomology, and Braid Group Actions, §§2a-2b, author pp. 8-9
references.locator: §2a opening graded-category paragraph, §2b through Theorem 2.2 proof, and §2c complex-category conventions, PDF pp.8–10, printed pp.9–11

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, ch. 3, §3.2, printed pp. 68-69
references.locator: §3.2 opening and Definition 3.2.1, PDF pp.2–3, printed pp.68–69

items.strategy: Write the B-action and the exact sequence 0→(ε)→B→k→0. Right k-flatness follows from vector-space exactness. If the quotient split B-linearly, the lift u of 1 would satisfy εu=0 and u mod ε=1, impossible since Ann_B(ε)=(ε). Tensor k gives the nonprojective output.
items.proof_strategy: direct

items.title: A left-projective tensor bimodule need not be right-flat
items.statement: Let B=k, A=k[ε]/(ε²) with trivial grading, and M=k with left k-action and right A-action through A→k. M is finite projective over B, but M⊗_A− does not preserve the monomorphism (ε)↪A in 0→(ε)→A→k→0: the induced map k⊗_A(ε)→k⊗_A A is zero although its source is k.

references.title: Stacks Project, Algebra, §10.12, tag 00CV
references.locator: §10.12 Remark 11 and Example 12

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, ch. 3, §3.2, printed pp. 68-69
references.locator: §3.2 opening and Definition 3.2.1, PDF pp.2–3, printed pp.68–69

items.strategy: Use ε·ε=0 to identify (ε) with the simple A-module k; identify k⊗_A(ε) and k⊗_A A with k using the tensor unit and quotient action. The inclusion sends 1⊗ε to 1⊗ε=ε·1⊗1=0, so exactness fails at the first arrow.
items.proof_strategy: direct

items.title: Complexes, homotopies and contractibility in an additive category
items.statement: For any additive category C, a cochain complex has d^n:C^n→C^{n+1} and d^{n+1}d^n=0; a cochain map commutes with d; a homotopy f−g=dh+hd has h^n:C^n→D^{n−1}. Reindexing C_n=C^{−n} gives chain differential degree −1 and chain homotopy degree +1. Contractibility means 1=dh+hd, and homotopy equivalence has a two-sided inverse up to this relation. Finite biproducts are degreewise. These notions use zero morphisms but do not assert homology objects without kernels/cokernels.

references.title: Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, ch.1 §§1.1, 1.2, 1.4
Clark–Morrison–Walker, Fixing the Functoriality of Khovanov Homology, Appendix A.1, printed pp.1562–1563
Bar-Natan, Fast Khovanov Homology Computations, §4 Lemma 4.2 and §5, printed pp.5–6

items.proof_strategy: Verify d² and the chain-map equations survive degreewise biproducts, using the published additive-complex proof. Reindex the published abelian-category chain homotopy/contractibility definitions and check the cochain formula and degree conversion. All formulas use only addition, negatives and zero morphisms.

items.title: An invertible cochain differential block and its candidate reduction
items.statement: For a cochain complex in an additive category, fix C^n=A⊕U and C^{n+1}=B⊕V with d^n=[[a,b],[c,φ]] (rows B,V; columns A,U) and an isomorphism φ:U→V. Define the candidate reduced arrows at degrees n−1,n,n+1 as p:C^{n−1}→A, a−bφ^{-1}c:A→B, and r:B→C^{n+2}, where d^{n−1}=[p;q] and d^{n+1}=[r,s]; keep all other objects/arrows. The next lemma verifies this is a complex. The homological convention is the same formula after n↦−n.

references.title: Bar-Natan, Fast Khovanov Homology Computations, §4 Lemma 4.2 and §5, printed pp.5–6
Clark–Morrison–Walker, Fixing the Functoriality of Khovanov Homology, Appendix A.1, printed pp.1562–1563

items.proof_strategy: Record all domains/codomains and the ordered block convention. Treat the Schur arrows as candidate data until the next lemma checks square-zero; this avoids assuming that a matrix formula automatically defines a complex.

items.title: Triangular basis changes diagonalize an invertible differential block
items.statement: With L=[[1,−bφ^{-1}],[0,1]] on B⊕V and R=[[1,0],[−φ^{-1}c,1]] on A⊕U, one has Ld^nR=diag(a−bφ^{-1}c,φ), with L^{-1}=[[1,bφ^{-1}],[0,1]] and R^{-1}=[[1,0],[φ^{-1}c,1]]. The transformed neighboring differentials are [p;0] and [r,0], and the reduced arrows square to zero.

references.title: Bar-Natan, Fast Khovanov Homology Computations, §4 Lemma 4.2 and §5, printed pp.5–6
Clark–Morrison–Walker, Fixing the Functoriality of Khovanov Homology, Appendix A.1, printed pp.1562–1563

items.proof_strategy: Multiply dR then LdR explicitly. From d^n[p;q]=0 obtain cp+φq=0; from [r,s]d^n=0 obtain rb+sφ=0. The transformed incoming arrow is R^{-1}[p;q]=[p;0] and the outgoing arrow is [r,s]L^{-1}=[r,0]. Consequently (a−bφ^{-1}c)p=0 and r(a−bφ^{-1}c)=0, including unbounded neighboring degrees.

items.title: Gaussian elimination splits a contractible two-term complex
items.statement: Under the preceding additive-category hypotheses, the original complex X is chain-isomorphic to Xbar⊕K, where Xbar is the Schur-complement reduction and K is 0→U --φ→ V→0 in degrees n,n+1. An isomorphism from X to Xbar⊕K has T^n=R^{-1}, T^{n+1}=L and identity components elsewhere, with inverse R,L^{-1}; K is contractible via φ^{-1}:V→U.

references.title: Bar-Natan, Fast Khovanov Homology Computations, §4 Lemma 4.2 and §5, printed pp.5–6
Clark–Morrison–Walker, Fixing the Functoriality of Khovanov Homology, Appendix A.1, printed pp.1562–1563

items.proof_strategy: Use the previous diagonal and neighboring-zero calculations to check T^{j+1}d_X^j=d_{Xbar⊕K}^jT^j in every degree, especially n−1 and n+1. Check inverse matrices and d_Kφ^{-1}+φ^{-1}d_K=1_K in its two nonzero degrees. Deletion is homotopy equivalence after the chain isomorphism, not equality of complexes.

items.title: Explicit strong deformation retract from Gaussian cancellation
items.statement: For X and Xbar, take p^n=[1,0], p^{n+1}=[1,−bφ^{-1}], i^n=[1;−φ^{-1}c], i^{n+1}=[1;0], with identity components elsewhere. Let h^{n+1}:B⊕V→A⊕U be [[0,0],[0,φ^{-1}]] and all other h^j zero. Then p,i are cochain maps, pi=1_Xbar, 1_X−ip=dh+hd, and ph=hi=h²=0.

references.title: Clark–Morrison–Walker, Fixing the Functoriality of Khovanov Homology, Appendix A.1, printed pp.1562–1563
Bar-Natan, Fast Khovanov Homology Computations, §4 Lemma 4.2 and §5, printed pp.5–6

items.proof_strategy: Conjugate inclusion/projection and the two-term contraction by the chain isomorphism, obtaining the displayed matrices. Directly compute pi in both degrees, compute 1−ip at n and n+1 as [[0,0],[φ^{-1}c,1]] and [[0,bφ^{-1}],[0,1]], match hd and dh respectively, and check each side condition by matrix multiplication.

items.title: Gaussian cancellation preserves homotopy type and abelian-category homology
items.statement: The chosen p and i are inverse in the homotopy category of complexes over every additive category. If the ambient category is abelian, they induce inverse isomorphisms on every homology object. The claim does not identify X and Xbar as complexes before splitting off the contractible summand.

references.title: Clark–Morrison–Walker, Fixing the Functoriality of Khovanov Homology, Appendix A.1, printed pp.1562–1563
Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, ch.1 §§1.1, 1.2, 1.4

items.proof_strategy: The homotopy assertion follows from pi=1 and 1−ip=dh+hd. In the abelian case use the valid published homology construction: for any homotopy term, its restriction to a cycle inclusion is d h and factors through the boundary image, so its induced homology map is zero. Hence H(pi)=1 and H(ip)=1 by functoriality. This proof avoids the published element-chase proof for arbitrary abelian categories.

items.title: Finite iteration of current invertible-block cancellations
items.statement: Any finite sequence of Gaussian cancellations in an additive category gives a strong deformation retract when each pivot is invertible in the current Schur-complement complex. If retracts compose as X⇄Y⇄Z, their data compose as p=p₂p₁, i=i₁i₂, h=h₁+i₁h₂p₁. A finite aggregate isomorphism Φ:U→V can instead be cancelled at once. Different valid choices yield homotopy-equivalent reductions, not generally equal or canonical complexes; no infinite iteration or guaranteed size decrease is asserted.

references.title: Bar-Natan, Fast Khovanov Homology Computations, §4 Lemma 4.2 and §5, printed pp.5–6
Clark–Morrison–Walker, Fixing the Functoriality of Khovanov Homology, Appendix A.1, printed pp.1562–1563

items.proof_strategy: Induct on the number of steps. Substitute the composite formulas into pi=1 and 1−ip=dh+hd, use chain-map equations and p₁i₁=1, then compute ph=hi=h²=0 using each retract side condition. Apply the single-pivot theorem to an aggregate invertible block. Compare reductions through the original complex to obtain homotopy equivalence without a confluence assertion.

items.title: Additive functors preserve chosen Gaussian cancellations
items.statement: An additive functor F between additive categories sends a chosen invertible-block cancellation to the corresponding cancellation of F(X), including the Schur differential and the images F(p),F(i),F(h) satisfying all strong-retract identities. No exactness is required. If the target is abelian, these image retract maps induce inverse homology isomorphisms. No comparison of F(H(X)) with H(F(X)) is asserted.

references.title: Clark–Morrison–Walker, Fixing the Functoriality of Khovanov Homology, Appendix A.1, printed pp.1562–1563
Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, ch.1 §§1.1, 1.2, 1.4

items.proof_strategy: Use preservation of finite biproducts, sums, negatives and zero morphisms to apply F entrywise to each finite matrix. Functoriality preserves φφ^{-1}=1, so F(φ^{-1})=F(φ)^{-1}. Apply F to the explicit differential, chain-isomorphism and retract equations. The published degreewise-functor proposition is abelian-only, so prove the additive extension directly.

items.title: Transferred maps are functorial up to homotopy, with strict naturality limits
items.statement: For chosen retracts (p_X,i_X,h_X) and (p_Y,i_Y,h_Y), transfer a cochain map f:X→Y by fbar=p_Y f i_X and a homotopy s by sbar=p_Y s i_X. Identity transfers strictly. For composable f:X→Y and g:Y→Z, (gf)bar−gbar fbar is null-homotopic by p_Z g h_Y f i_X. Thus transfer is functorial on homotopy classes, but need not be a strict functor on cochain maps. Strict naturality holds for morphisms commuting with the chosen retract data; no choice-free naturality or confluence is claimed.

references.title: Clark–Morrison–Walker, Fixing the Functoriality of Khovanov Homology, Appendix A.1, printed pp.1562–1563
Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, ch.1 §§1.1, 1.2, 1.4

items.proof_strategy: Check fbar and sbar against differentials using that p and i are cochain maps. Expand (gf)bar−gbar fbar=p_Z g(1−i_Yp_Y)f i_X=p_Z g(dh_Y+h_Yd)f i_X, so the homotopy is +p_Z g h_Y f i_X with this difference convention; if comparing gbar fbar−(gf)bar it is the displayed negative. Make the sign convention explicit in the authored proof. Since p_Xi_X=1, identity transfers exactly. A strict comparison follows when f and g commute with i and p.

items.title: A unit pivot forces the minus Schur sign
items.statement: Over Q consider the two-term cochain complex Q²→Q² with matrix [[1,1],[1,1]] and cancel the lower-right identity. The correct Schur differential is 1−1·1^{-1}·1=0 on Q→Q, matching one-dimensional kernel and cokernel. A plus sign gives multiplication by 2 and wrongly makes both homology groups zero.

references.title: Bar-Natan, Fast Khovanov Homology Computations, §4 Lemma 4.2 and §5, printed pp.5–6
Clark–Morrison–Walker, Fixing the Functoriality of Khovanov Homology, Appendix A.1, printed pp.1562–1563

items.proof_strategy: Compute d² automatically for the two-term complex, find ker(d)=span(1,−1), coker(d)≅Q, and compare with the zero reduced differential. Compute the erroneous +2 map and its zero kernel/cokernel.

items.title: Neighboring differentials transform with the pivot basis changes
items.statement: Over any field k, the cochain segment k --[1;−1]→ k² --[[1,1],[1,1]]→ k² --[1,−1]→ k has both neighboring composites zero. Cancel the lower-right identity; the transformed arrows are [1;0], diag(0,1), and [1,0], leaving the reduced segment k --1→ k --0→ k --1→ k.

references.title: Bar-Natan, Fast Khovanov Homology Computations, §4 Lemma 4.2 and §5, printed pp.5–6
Clark–Morrison–Walker, Fixing the Functoriality of Khovanov Homology, Appendix A.1, printed pp.1562–1563

items.proof_strategy: Multiply the original neighboring matrices to get zero. Use R^{-1}=[[1,0],[1,1]] and L^{-1}=[[1,1],[0,1]] for a=b=c=φ=1; compute R^{-1}[1;−1]=[1;0], LdR=diag(0,1), and [1,−1]L^{-1}=[1,0], then verify both reduced composites are zero.

items.title: Two adjacent noncomposable Gaussian pivots in either finite order
items.statement: Use the CMW Lemma A.2 shape A→B⊕C→D₁⊕D₂⊕E→F⊕G→H, with the B→D₁ entry ψ and E→G entry φ both isomorphisms and consecutive differentials squaring to zero. If the middle matrices are [[ψ,β],[x,γ],[y,δ]] and [[z,μ,λ],[w,ν,φ]], cancellation in either order leaves A→C→D₂→F→H with middle arrows γ−xψ^{-1}β and μ−λφ^{-1}ν, and yields composite retract data by the finite-iteration formula. This is an order comparison for this configuration only.

references.title: Clark–Morrison–Walker, Fixing the Functoriality of Khovanov Homology, Appendix A.1, printed pp.1562–1563
Bar-Natan, Fast Khovanov Homology Computations, §4 Lemma 4.2 and §5, printed pp.5–6

items.proof_strategy: First cancel ψ and calculate C→D₂⊕E as [γ−xψ^{-1}β;δ−yψ^{-1}β], with φ still an unchanged current pivot; then cancel φ and obtain D₂→F as μ−λφ^{-1}ν. Reverse the steps: cancel φ first, leaving D₁⊕D₂→F as [z−λφ^{-1}w,μ−λφ^{-1}ν] with ψ still invertible, then cancel ψ. Print p₂p₁,i₁i₂,h₁+i₁h₂p₁ for each order and verify side conditions from the theorem; account for end arrows by d²=0.

items.title: The isolated differential 2 on the integers cannot be cancelled
items.statement: The two-term complex 0→Z --2→ Z→0 has a noninvertible differential entry and H^{n+1}≅Z/2. Deleting both terms would produce the zero complex and erase that homology; 2 has no inverse Z→Z.

references.title: Bar-Natan, Fast Khovanov Homology Computations, §4 Lemma 4.2 and §5, printed pp.5–6
Clark–Morrison–Walker, Fixing the Functoriality of Khovanov Homology, Appendix A.1, printed pp.1562–1563

items.proof_strategy: Compute ker(2)=0 and coker(2)=Z/2 in Ab. If an integral inverse existed, 2u=1 for some integer u, impossible. Therefore the pivot hypothesis is genuinely needed.

items.title: Gaussian transfer is not strictly functorial on arbitrary cochain maps
items.statement: Let Y and K each be the two-term identity cochain complex k --1→ k, let X=Y⊕K, and cancel K so Xbar=Y. Let f:X→X send Y isomorphically to K and kill K; let g:X→X send K isomorphically to Y and kill Y. Their individual transfers to Y vanish, but the transfer of gf is 1_Y, a nonzero chain map. Because Y is contractible, this discrepancy is null-homotopic.

references.title: Clark–Morrison–Walker, Fixing the Functoriality of Khovanov Homology, Appendix A.1, printed pp.1562–1563

items.proof_strategy: Write f and g as off-diagonal 2×2 matrices in both degrees and check they commute with the identity differentials. With the standard projection/inclusion, pfi=0 and pgi=0 whereas pgfi=1_Y. The identity on Y has contraction h^{n+1}=1_k, proving homotopy-class functoriality survives.
